factors.name: Coherent Operating Inflection Assimilation
factors.description: Detects fresh, standardized changes in revenue growth and operating margin, retains only sign-coherent operating inflections, and discounts events that have already generated a large short-run return. The final signal is industry-demeaned and cross-sectionally ranked, with positive values representing unassimilated positive operating inflections.
factors.trading_idea: A simultaneous acceleration in reported revenue growth and operating margin is a more credible change in operating trajectory than either accounting field alone. When this coherent quarterly inflection arrives without a commensurate three-day price response, investors and analysts have not fully incorporated its implications for forward earnings, allowing a six-day post-disclosure drift. The hypothesis is falsifiable: subsequent returns should align with the signed operating inflection only for fresh, coherent updates with muted initial price assimilation, and should be negligible after already-large immediate moves. The edge can persist because interpreting whether a margin move is demand-led, rather than a transient cost effect, requires slower fundamental-model revision rather than mechanical news trading.

factors.name: Fresh Inventory Turnover Assimilation Gap
factors.description: Computes a quarter-over-quarter change in log revenue-to-inventory at fresh fundamental updates, then compares its cross-sectional rank with the rank of the contemporaneous abnormal stock return. The signal remains active only for twelve bars after the disclosure update.
factors.trading_idea: A disclosed increase in revenue relative to inventory is a compact accounting identity for improving inventory productivity, without requiring fragile assumptions about margin, cash-flow, or clearance motives. The child goes long positive turnover updates that received an unusually muted same-day price response and short deteriorations that were insufficiently discounted, targeting delayed assimilation of a readily observable but cognitively secondary operating metric. This is falsifiable: conditional on fresh fundamental updates, the return effect should be strongest for the largest turnover-versus-price-reaction gaps and should vanish when the market has already reacted proportionally; the lag can persist because investors prioritize headline revenue and EPS over balance-sheet operating efficiency.

factors.name: Fresh Dual-Surprise Attention Shortfall
factors.description: Uses one-day changes in point-in-time EPS and revenue surprises to identify fresh, concordant report deliveries without treating ordinary price movement as a fundamental update. It weights the signed surprise by the gap between the event-day return and pre-event volatility, discounting events already accompanied by unusually high turnover.
factors.trading_idea: The child isolates the first daily bar on which both EPS and revenue-surprise fields update concordantly, then buys positive deliveries and shorts negative deliveries only when the immediate price response is muted relative to pre-event volatility and event-day attention is low. This targets the early portion of post-earnings information diffusion rather than the parent’s broader five-day displacement, so it should realize its payoff within the fixed six-day horizon. The edge can persist because interpreting two financial-statement channels and reallocating institutional portfolios takes several sessions, especially when limited turnover indicates that the announcement has not yet reached broad ownership; it is falsified if muted, low-turnover dual-surprise events do not outperform fully reacted or high-attention matched events over the next six days.

factors.name: Valuation-Sensitive Cash-Cycle Repricing
factors.description: Computes fresh point-in-time changes in cash conversion cycle, scaled by the prior cycle, and weights the inverse change by cross-sectional revenue-growth and EV/sales ranks. The event impulse decays causally so the factor remains active while the filing implication is incorporated.
factors.trading_idea: A fresh widening of the cash-conversion cycle is adverse evidence when paired with strong reported revenue growth: it can indicate that sales are being financed through receivables or inventory rather than converted into cash. The effect should be strongest for expensive firms, where valuation embeds a long-duration growth narrative that is sensitive to evidence of weaker cash realization; the signal therefore longs cash-cycle improvements and shorts cash-cycle deteriorations conditional on revenue growth and EV/sales. This is falsifiable: six-day returns after cash-cycle updates should be monotonically lower for high-growth, high-EV/sales firms with the largest cycle widening, and the effect should weaken for low-valuation firms; it can persist because parsing working-capital detail from filings is slower and more uncertain than reacting to headline revenue.

factors.name: Fresh Surprise Yield Reaction Gap
factors.description: On days when epsSurprise changes, ranks the current EPS surprise scaled by price and subtracts the rank of the stock's same-day return. High values identify favorable earnings news receiving unusually weak immediate price confirmation; low values identify bad news receiving unusually strong or insufficiently negative confirmation.
factors.trading_idea: New earnings-surprise information is not fully incorporated when the cross-sectional magnitude of the surprise is large but the contemporaneous price response is muted or moves in the opposite direction. The signal measures this report-day information-to-price-response gap, rather than carrying stale quarterly growth levels for months. The edge should persist because institutional estimate revisions, portfolio rebalancing, and interpretation of earnings quality occur over several sessions, while arbitrageurs face event-timing noise and uncertainty about whether an initial muted reaction reflects delayed assimilation or genuinely unimportant news. Falsifiably, positive-gap observations should earn positive six-bar returns and negative-gap observations negative returns, with the effect concentrated on fresh earnings-surprise updates rather than non-event days.

factors.name: Cash Realization Margin Innovation
factors.description: Ranks only newly disclosed year-over-year changes in operating-cash-flow margin, where cash margin is operating cash flow divided by revenue. The signal is zero between disclosures so it expresses a fresh accounting-information event rather than a persistent stale fundamental level.
factors.trading_idea: A fresh year-over-year improvement in operating-cash-flow margin signals that reported sales are converting into cash more efficiently, capturing a broad improvement in demand quality, pricing, or working-capital discipline without requiring a brittle inventory-clearance narrative. Investors often initially prioritize headline revenue and EPS, while the implications of a changed cash realization rate require statement-level interpretation and are incorporated more gradually after the filing. The hypothesis is falsified if positive fresh cash-margin innovations do not produce higher six-bar returns than negative innovations, especially after excluding stale quarterly observations.

factors.name: Sales-Earnings Polarity Reassessment
factors.description: On fresh quarterly disclosures, the factor identifies opposite-signed standardized EPS and revenue surprises. It ranks negative EPS surprises accompanied by positive revenue surprises highest, and positive EPS surprises accompanied by negative revenue surprises lowest.
factors.trading_idea: An EPS surprise that conflicts in sign with the contemporaneous revenue surprise is more likely to reflect transient margin, expense timing, or accounting classification than a durable change in customer demand. Headline-oriented trading initially emphasizes EPS, while investors and analysts take several days to reconcile whether the sales signal validates the earnings result; therefore, positive-EPS/negative-revenue conflicts should underperform and negative-EPS/positive-revenue conflicts should recover over six days. The edge can persist because revenue-versus-EPS reconciliation requires processing two disclosure channels and is not the primary objective of immediate earnings-event traders. This is falsified if, conditional on fresh conflicting releases, six-day returns are not increasing from positive-EPS/negative-revenue cases to negative-EPS/positive-revenue cases.

factors.name: Disclosed Operating-Cycle Efficiency Impulse
factors.description: On each newly available operating-cycle disclosure, the factor measures the percentage reduction versus the immediately preceding disclosed value. It ranks only fresh improvements cross-sectionally and sector-neutralizes the result, assigning zero outside disclosure updates.
factors.trading_idea: A newly disclosed reduction in the operating cycle is a broad, direct measure of improved cash efficiency: firms are collecting receivables faster, turning inventory faster, or requiring less capital to sustain sales. Unlike the parent’s second-difference growth spread, this signal acts only when a new accounting observation arrives and therefore does not repeatedly trade a stale quarterly value. The edge should persist because investors often process headline earnings and revenue before decomposing the balance-sheet implications for future free-cash-flow generation; it is falsified if sector-neutral operating-cycle reductions do not predict positive six-bar returns, especially after controlling for contemporaneous revenue growth.

factors.name: Inventory Efficiency Margin Update Drift
factors.description: Ranks fresh quarterly disclosure updates where both log inventory turnover and gross margin increase versus the immediately preceding disclosed state. The combined update is sector-neutralized before cross-sectional ranking, and names without a joint update receive zero exposure.
factors.trading_idea: A simultaneous disclosed increase in inventory turnover and gross margin is a compact confirmation that sales are being converted efficiently rather than generated through discount-led clearance. Investors often process the headline growth narrative and margin result before fully incorporating the operational implication of faster inventory conversion, producing a short post-disclosure drift. The edge should persist because the two-accounting-line confirmation is infrequent, sector-specific, and costly to arbitrage before the filing; it is falsifiable if positive six-day returns do not concentrate in names with jointly positive turnover and margin updates.

factors.name: Unpaid Intangible Capital-Efficiency Update (jitter)
factors.description: Detects fresh quarter-scale ROIC changes, standardizes each firm's update against its own trailing history, and subtracts the recent volatility-scaled price response. The resulting unpriced update is decayed over several days and weighted toward intangible-intensive firms.
factors.trading_idea: A fresh improvement in ROIC is especially informative for intangible-heavy firms because reported capital efficiency helps investors infer whether previously expensed research, software, and brand investment is becoming economically productive. The signal buys positive ROIC innovations and shorts negative innovations only when the contemporaneous three-day price response has not already incorporated the update. The hypothesis is falsifiable: the six-day IC should be positive on fresh ROIC-update observations, should weaken materially after a large same-direction initial return, and should be negligible away from disclosure updates. The edge can persist because decomposing a quarterly efficiency change into genuine intangible monetization versus accounting noise is costly and is incorporated gradually by fundamental investors.

factors.name: Tax-Regime Gated Operating Diffusion (jitter)
factors.description: Ranks fresh signed revenue-growth and operating-margin changes only when their direction agrees with a cross-sectional tax-and-cash credibility state, and discounts disclosures already accompanied by a large industry-relative price reaction. Eligible scores are held through the six-bar post-filing assimilation interval.
factors.trading_idea: A coherent revenue-growth and operating-margin inflection is most tradable when the tax-and-cash disclosure state confirms that the reported earnings change is economically distributable: improving operations should be paired with strong cash realization and a non-worsening tax burden, while deteriorating operations should be paired with weak cash realization and a rising tax burden. Parent B's realized sign suggests that tax/cash headlines are not generally short-horizon reversal opportunities; instead, they classify whether the market is facing a persistent earnings-quality regime, so they should gate rather than fade Parent A's operating signal. The interaction creates edge because price underreaction to an operating inflection is more credible when the contemporaneous tax settlement state resolves whether the margin change represents cash-generative economics or a potentially misleading accounting outcome.

factors.name: Self-Financed Research Transition
factors.description: Ranks industry-relative combinations of quarterly R&D-intensity step-ups and current free-cash-flow coverage of R&D expense. It favors firms increasing research spending while retaining internally funded investment capacity.
factors.trading_idea: A rise in R&D intensity is economically informative only when the firm can fund the additional research from internally generated free cash flow rather than external capital. Such firms have both the option to sustain investment through uncertainty and a lower probability that reported R&D acceleration reflects distress or promotional spending. The hypothesis is falsified if, within industries, firms with jointly high R&D-intensity increases and FCF-to-R&D coverage do not outperform low-coverage R&D accelerators over the next six bars. The edge can persist because investors often react to the visible R&D expense immediately while incorporating the durability of its funding source more slowly from quarterly cash-flow statements.

factors.name: Collection Cycle Repricing (jitter)
factors.description: Ranks firms by the negative of the point-in-time year-over-year change in days sales outstanding. Higher values identify firms whose collection cycle improved or deteriorated least, while lower values identify worsening cash collection.
factors.trading_idea: A year-over-year increase in days sales outstanding indicates that reported revenue is being converted into cash more slowly, often because customers require looser payment terms or because collection quality has deteriorated. Equity investors tend to initially emphasize the reported revenue and earnings release, while the working-capital implication is incorporated more gradually as subsequent cash-flow evidence arrives. The hypothesis is falsifiable: firms with the largest disclosed DSO increases should underperform firms with stable or falling DSO over the following six trading days, including after controlling for sector. The edge can persist because interpreting receivables aging requires accounting attention and is noisier than reacting to headline earnings figures.

factors.name: Quarterly Share-Count Supply
factors.description: Cross-sectional rank of negative point-in-time share-count growth. High scores identify firms with lower dilution or stronger net share retirement.
factors.trading_idea: This child changes mechanism rather than retuning the parent’s cash-conversion signal: disclosed share-count growth measures net equity supply, while declining share count reflects a credible reduction in the public claim on future earnings. Investors often focus on reported operating results and incorporate dilution or repurchase implications more gradually, while issuers cannot instantly remove the supply pressure created by financing decisions. The edge is falsified if low disclosed share growth does not predict relatively positive six-bar returns after controlling for market capitalization and contemporaneous profitability.

factors.name: Rollover Cash-Truth Absorption Polarity
factors.description: Ranks stressed positive-report events by the interaction of cash-backed earnings quality, denominator assistance, short-run price reaction, and persistent high-volume range-compressed candle absorption. It is long cash-supported refinancing resolutions with sell-side absorption and short cosmetic EPS rallies with buy-side absorption.
factors.trading_idea: A cash-backed positive earnings surprise matters most when a firm is facing a worsening short-term refinancing burden, but negative close-location absorption after the report indicates that sellers are being accommodated without price clearance, leaving the favorable refinancing resolution under-recognized. Conversely, a buyback-assisted EPS beat accompanied by a rallied, high-volume compressed close near the bar high is interpreted as buyers being absorbed by latent supply rather than genuine acceptance of improved funding capacity. This interaction has edge because the fundamental state identifies whether the headline is economically credible, while the absorption polarity identifies whether the market's initial order flow is concealment of demand/supply rather than efficient price discovery.

factors.name: DuPont-Concordant Reaction Gap
factors.description: Ranks the gap between a fresh ROIC update and its volatility-scaled two-day price response. Signals are active only when operating-margin and asset-turnover updates have the same sign as the ROIC update.
factors.trading_idea: A reported ROIC improvement is more economically credible when both operating margin and asset turnover improve in the same direction, because this separates genuine operating execution from a mechanical capital-base or accounting-denominator change. The child buys positive concordant operating updates, and shorts negative ones, only when the contemporaneous two-day price response has not reflected the cross-sectional magnitude of the ROIC change. The edge should persist for several days because investors must reconcile multiple quarterly accounting channels rather than reacting to a single headline metric; it is falsified if concordant updates do not outperform discordant ROIC changes after controlling for the initial price reaction.

factors.name: Stale-Filing Quiet Excursion Reversal (jitter)
factors.description: Sector-residualized five-day price moves are faded only during a mature interval since the last revenue or operating-cash-flow update, with high-volume moves down-weighted as more likely informational. Higher signal values correspond to negative quiet excursions expected to rebound.
factors.trading_idea: The parent’s static accounting-credibility valuation state is too slow and can be directionally dominated by short-run repricing, as indicated by its increasingly negative IC at longer horizons. This child instead identifies price excursions occurring well after the last revenue or operating-cash-flow disclosure, when investors are anchored to stale fundamentals and a low-volume move is more likely to reflect temporary attention or inventory pressure than new information. The edge should persist because quarterly disclosure gaps cannot be arbitraged away continuously, while low-participation price pressure is costly and uncertain to distinguish from information in real time.

factors.name: Candle Absorption Pressure Filter (jitter)
factors.description: Computes a causal latent-pressure state from signed close location, abnormal volume, and range compression relative to each stock's trailing range. High-volume, low-range bars receive greater evidential weight, and the final score rewards persistent directional absorption rather than a single large price move.
factors.trading_idea: Daily bars contain a noisy observation of latent one-sided trading pressure: a close near the bar high or low is directional evidence, while unusually high volume combined with an unusually compressed range indicates that liquidity providers are absorbing rather than fully clearing that pressure. A causal evidence filter accumulates only these absorbed directional observations and discounts isolated, high-impact moves; persistent latent pressure should predict continuation over the next six bars as the parent order or information diffusion remains unfinished. The hypothesis is falsified if high-volume compressed directional bars reverse as often as similarly directional bars with ordinary volume and range, or if persistence of the filtered state does not improve six-bar return ranking.

factors.name: Turnover Margin Confirmation
factors.description: Ranks firms by the average of quarter-over-quarter changes in inventory turnover and gross margin. It is long companies with jointly improving sell-through efficiency and unit economics, and short companies with joint deterioration.
factors.trading_idea: Inventory reduction is economically favorable only when it reflects faster sell-through rather than discounting. Firms reporting simultaneous improvements in inventory turnover and gross margin provide a simple, independently verifiable confirmation of demand and operating efficiency that investors may incorporate gradually after a filing. The edge should persist because the two accounting measures are released discretely and require cross-statement interpretation, while the falsifiable prediction is that the positive six-day return spread is concentrated in firms with both turnover and margin improvements, not either metric alone.

factors.name: Receivable-Conversion Rally Fade (jitter)
factors.description: Shorts stocks with a positive ten-day abnormal rally only when receivables growth exceeds revenue growth and income quality has deteriorated versus the prior disclosed quarter. The factor uses the minimum of the two cross-sectional adverse-evidence ranks to require corroboration rather than multiplying many accounting branches.
factors.trading_idea: Sales growth is less credible when receivables are growing faster than revenue while operating-cash conversion is deteriorating, because reported demand may reflect looser credit or revenue recognition rather than cash-generative sell-through. A sustained rally in this state is prone to a six-day correction as investors process the working-capital evidence and marginal buyers lose confidence in the headline growth narrative. The effect should persist because quarterly cash-collection detail is costly to interpret and is incorporated more slowly than a visible price rally; falsifiably, the negative post-rally return spread should be concentrated in names with both adverse collection signals, and should be weak when either signal is absent.

factors.name: Phase-Oriented Demand Transmission
factors.description: Computes rolling standardized return and log-volume innovations, then estimates whether lagged volume predicts returns more strongly than lagged returns predict volume. The factor is high when a current positive volume innovation occurs in a volume-leading regime, and low for negative volume shocks or price-leading regimes.
factors.trading_idea: A volume shock is informative only when the recent return-volume system shows that volume innovations tend to lead price innovations rather than merely react to them. The signal estimates the directional asymmetry of this lag relationship and takes the sign of the current volume surprise, treating persistent volume-leading-price dynamics as latent demand transmission that should continue over the next several sessions. This is falsified if positive volume surprises do not predict positive returns specifically in positive lead-orientation regimes, or if the effect is equally strong when price leads volume; it can persist because traders observe aggregate daily volume but cannot directly distinguish informed execution from reactive liquidity without estimating this rolling phase relation.

factors.name: Climactic Cash Delivery Rejection
factors.description: Ranks fresh positive revenue-growth and cash-margin updates by pre-report appreciation, abnormal disclosure-day volume, and intrabar rejection. High scores identify pre-priced delivery events where a volume climax closes near the low and are expected to precede negative returns.
factors.trading_idea: A positive revenue-growth and operating-cash-flow-margin update is bearish over the next six days only when the disclosure bar reveals immediate distribution: unusually high participation but a close near the intraday low. This conditions the parent's slow post-filing unwind on observable evidence that pre-positioned holders are already selling into confirmation, bringing the reversal forward to the fixed six-bar horizon. The edge can persist because interpreting cash-quality disclosures and distinguishing informed distribution from ordinary earnings volume is operationally costly, while institutional liquidation is typically executed over several sessions. Falsifiably, the negative six-bar spread should be concentrated in positive cash-confirmed updates with both volume shocks and poor close location, and should be weak or absent for equally positive updates that close strongly.

factors.name: Collection Cycle Repricing (jitter)
factors.description: Ranks firms by the negative of the point-in-time year-over-year change in days sales outstanding. Higher values identify firms whose collection cycle improved or deteriorated least, while lower values identify worsening cash collection.
factors.trading_idea: A year-over-year increase in days sales outstanding indicates that reported revenue is being converted into cash more slowly, often because customers require looser payment terms or because collection quality has deteriorated. Equity investors tend to initially emphasize the reported revenue and earnings release, while the working-capital implication is incorporated more gradually as subsequent cash-flow evidence arrives. The hypothesis is falsifiable: firms with the largest disclosed DSO increases should underperform firms with stable or falling DSO over the following six trading days, including after controlling for sector. The edge can persist because interpreting receivables aging requires accounting attention and is noisier than reacting to headline earnings figures.

factors.name: Cash-Cycle Duration Repricing
factors.description: Ranks firms by the quarter-over-quarter reduction in cash conversion cycle duration. Missing or insufficiently seasoned fundamental observations are assigned a neutral score.
factors.trading_idea: A disclosed shortening of the cash-conversion cycle is a parsimonious measure of improving operating efficiency: cash is tied up in receivables and inventory for less time, reducing external-financing needs and increasing the durability of reported earnings. Investors often treat quarterly working-capital changes as accounting noise and wait for confirmation in subsequent filings, so the information can diffuse over the following week. The hypothesis is falsified if firms with the largest point-in-time quarter-over-quarter cash-cycle reductions do not earn higher six-bar forward returns, or if the effect disappears after controlling for contemporaneous operating performance.

factors.name: R&D Gross-Profit Conversion State (jitter) (jitter) (jitter)
factors.description: Ranks firms by the interaction of a quarterly-scale increase in R&D-to-revenue and cross-sectional gross-profit growth. High R&D-intensity step-ups receive positive scores only when gross-profit growth is above the contemporaneous cross-sectional median.
factors.trading_idea: R&D spending is valuable when an increase in research intensity coincides with unusually strong gross-profit growth, which is a cleaner near-term indication that product investment is converting into economically valuable demand rather than merely raising expenses. The signal deliberately removes the parent's multi-branch cash-flow and margin gates, treating gross-profit conversion as the single conditioning state rather than attempting to forecast every operating outcome. The edge should persist because investors often classify an R&D step-up as a profitability drag before repeated gross-profit evidence makes commercialization visible in standard valuation screens; it is falsified if R&D step-ups with high relative gross-profit growth do not outperform similarly sized step-ups with weak gross-profit growth over the next six bars.

factors.name: R&D Gross-Profit Conversion State (jitter) (jitter)
factors.description: Ranks firms by the interaction of a quarterly-scale increase in R&D-to-revenue and cross-sectional gross-profit growth. High R&D-intensity step-ups receive positive scores only when gross-profit growth is above the contemporaneous cross-sectional median.
factors.trading_idea: R&D spending is valuable when an increase in research intensity coincides with unusually strong gross-profit growth, which is a cleaner near-term indication that product investment is converting into economically valuable demand rather than merely raising expenses. The signal deliberately removes the parent's multi-branch cash-flow and margin gates, treating gross-profit conversion as the single conditioning state rather than attempting to forecast every operating outcome. The edge should persist because investors often classify an R&D step-up as a profitability drag before repeated gross-profit evidence makes commercialization visible in standard valuation screens; it is falsified if R&D step-ups with high relative gross-profit growth do not outperform similarly sized step-ups with weak gross-profit growth over the next six bars.

factors.name: Cash-Conversion Step Attention Drift
factors.description: Ranks fresh EPS surprises after scaling their magnitude by the quarter-over-quarter change in operating-cash-flow coverage of net income and by low report-day volume relative to the stock's own trailing volume. Positive surprises with improving conversion receive higher scores, while negative surprises with deteriorating conversion receive lower scores.
factors.trading_idea: An earnings surprise is more durable when the accompanying filing shows that cash conversion has improved versus the prior reported state, rather than merely remaining positive. This incremental confirmation requires comparing two statement vintages and is most likely to be processed slowly when report-day turnover is low, so the signal targets delayed fundamental assimilation rather than the parent’s immediate reaction gap. The edge should persist because fast headline traders react to EPS while slower fundamental investors reconcile cash generation across filings; it is falsified if cash-conversion improvements do not amplify six-day post-report drift specifically in low-attention releases.
